To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the land cover and land use changes are not uniform across space and time; (ii) the land use change patterns differ between the study sites and between the different land uses; (iii) the land use changes are driven by a variety of factors including the availability of land and the availability of water; and (iv) the land use patterns are influenced by the land use policies of the local and national government.

(1) the spatial distribution of deforestation in southern Burkina Faso is related to a combination of environmental, social, and economic factors and is not the result of a simple cause-and-effect relationship; and (2) the spatial distribution is also related to the location and timing of migration, which is influenced by the economic and social factors that affect deforestation.
the use of remote sensing data in combination with GIS and statistics is an important and promising methodological tool for land use and land cover studies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of GIS to analyze and map land-use/cover change.
the development of a methodology to analyse land cover and land use dynamics.
the use of remote sensing data and GIS to analyse and interpret the spatial patterns and temporal dynamics of landscape change and human-environment interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the remote sensing imagery in the context of the GIS is a useful and effective tool for the analysis of the land use and land cover changes.

the use of the GIS and the statistical analysis of data from remote sensing images, and the combination of the results of the two approaches, is very useful for understanding the dynamics of land occupation and land use, and for the interpretation of the interactions between human activities and natural processes.
the use of GIS and remote sensing data is not a substitute for fieldwork.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is an attempt to integrate remote sensing, GIS, and statistical techniques to study the dynamics of land use and land cover change.
we have shown how the combination of remote sensing, GIS and statistics can be applied in a systematic way for the study of land use and land cover dynamics at different spatial and temporal scales.
we have shown that a combination of GIS, image analysis and statistics is an efficient tool to analyze land cover and land use change processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of remote sensing data, geographic information systems, and statistical analysis is not limited to mapping and that it can be applied in the analysis and interpretation of landscape dynamics.
the integration of remote sensing and GIS with statistics provides a powerful tool for analyzing land cover change, especially at the local scale.

the integration of remote sensing and GIS with statistical analysis is an effective way to analyze the dynamics of land use and occupation, especially when the goal is to study the interaction between human activities and natural processes.
